notes.title: New update for Creature Lab - more limbs and QoL features
notes.notes:
Hi, ingenious creature manufacturers!

After some time working on other projects, our team has returned to Creature Lab for some long-term support! In this update, we prepared a brilliant concoction of new limbs, a new combat log, and bugfixes.

We're happy to see that most progression issues seem to have been fixed. While there are still some errors lurking about, these prove difficult to identify and eliminate. If you encounter any issues with your save files, please [url=https://discord.com/invite/Gt8yt48mee]send them to us on our Discord server[/url].

With that in mind, our main goal was to give you new tools to play around with. We also realized that it's not always clear why certain creatures perform better or worse so we added a combat log for some extra clarity.

Check out the new limbs below:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/5c55afc7fde3c2bbbcdd49edd85e811192685fe0.png[/img]

The patch introduces the following changes:
[list]
[*] Added the Dragon Arm - a balanced limb unlocked late in the campaign.
[*] Added the Root Arm - an anti-light limb unlocked early in the campaign.
[*] Added the Crab Arm - an anti-armor limb unlocked in the middle of the campaign.
[*] Body chambers now have an additional light that turns on when the player looks directly at creatures contained within.
[*] Fixed an issue with some achievements not unlocking despite meeting the requirements.
[*] Improved some of the translations that displayed incorrect text.
[*] Implemented a new combat log that allows the player to see what happens during combat.
[*] Changed the battle and mission report screens to fit the new combat log files.
[/list]

notes.title: A new Sanbox Mode + a free 18+ DLC for Creature Lab available now!
notes.notes:
Hi, tireless fringe experimentators!

[b]The long-awaited big update for Creature Lab is in![/b] And it will allow you to tinker with nearly every aspect of your playthrough with the [b]Sandbox Mode[/b]. You can make it easier, you can make it harder, and you can do a bit of cheating to have fun with the game your way!

Some of you had the chance to test the main attraction - Sandbox Mode - during playtests and we're grateful for your feedback. Now the full mode is available for your pleasure. We hope you will enjoy it tremendously. We also added a large variety of fixes. You can check in the patch notes at the end of this post.

[quote] For the most stable experience with new features, we advise creating new save files. The new features will work with other saves, but a new save guarantees the best performance. [/quote]

But this is not all we have in store for you today! We even have an adult-only surprise courtesy of Madmind Studio. [b]Thanks to this cooperation, the main character of their acclaimed title Succubus is available to you in a free 18+ DLC as an exclusive creature![/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/985830/SUCCUBUS/

[h2]A new Sanbox Mode + a free 18+ DLC for Creature Lab available now![/h2]

Please enjoy a snippet of our new features with this teaser trailer:

[previewyoutube=1xmcMHFHnYE;full][/previewyoutube]

So what exactly will you get today for your enjoyment? Let's sum it up!

[h3]Sanbox Mode[/h3] allows you to set a large number of parameters to your liking. You can start a new game in Sanbox Mode or move your existing playtrough to Sanbox Mode. Among many things, you can:
[list]
[*] set the investigation multiplier and panic multiplier,
[*] set the investigation and panic to the selected value during gameplay,
[*] set the total population on the map and its weekly increase,
[*] opt for instant limb creation,
[*] opt for universal mutant DNA,
[*] get unlimited Dark Web tokens,
[*] spawn random element, elixir, mutagen, or body.
[/list]
Using Sandbox Mode parameter settings, you can tailor your game to anything you want and have unlimited fun in whatever way you like.

[quote] Please be mindful that choosing the Sanbox Mode turns off the Story Mode. You also cannot get achievements when playing in Sandbox Mode. [/quote]
[h3]New visual effects on creatures[/h3] 
You may notice that your creatures got... more colorful. Or that they have horns or strange growths on their bodies. Or maybe became slightly electric, or are oozing pretty visible clouds of stank. Yes, your creatures just got much more mutated. Now they acquire new visual effects based on their composition. In addition to existing possibilities with limb swaps, you can create some truly bizarre monsters. Because even mad scientists need diverse looks for their favorite creations!

[h3]Free 18+ Succubus DLC[/h3]
Want to spice up your gameplay? Thanks to our collaboration with Madmind Studio, you can add a true queen of Hell to your creature roster! She can spawn in the body chamber in place of the mutant you were making, so be on watch for this hellish beauty. The more mutants you make, the higher the chance for her to appear. The Succubus is as imposing as it is alluring. She will surely stand out from your collection of more corpse-like creatures. Of course, she also works as any other creature, which means you can upgrade her with different limbs as well! That also means you can grow her limbs in the incubator as well.

[b]The Succubus DLC can be downloaded separately here:[/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2447620/Creature_Lab__Succubus_Monster_Pack/


[b]Patch notes for the update:[/b]
[list]
[*] Added Sandbox Mode

[*] Fixed map freeze during sending mutants/scientists on a mission

This weekend, you will be able to delve into it and thoroughly check key features that we want to offer in an upcoming big update of Creature Lab. Please report any issues you will find in the build, as well as share your thoughts on the mode itself - we have prepared a special survey accessible straight from the game.

Of course, each of you will find at least some bumps on the road, so all the bug reports are super important to us. Let's iron out the Sandbox Mode together to make it a great experience!

notes.title: Scientist log - 015
notes.notes:
[i]As I remarked before, sometimes even a brilliant mind can use some "external help". Thanks to Dark Web, I can take up orders for the delivery of specific substances, limbs, and creatures from several not-very-public organizations working in the underground world of our city. One of the most important things that I can get from these commissions are favors from those shadowy groups - which I neatly register in my computer system as Tokens.[/i]

[h2]Tokens and what can you achieve with them[/h2]

[i]In general, I could group the Tokens received for various jobs into two groups - those who give the instant effect of some kind, a one-time event if you wish (sometimes pretty bloody, too), and those who are in work for one day. Let's say that it's a one-day-long boost to some of my activities, courtesy of my business partners. Every Token is limited in its scope for one district - except for two which have an overall effect on the panic level and military investigation progress.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/dc683aaa333d62bdff84415fb1cddaf364974839.gif[/img]

[i][b]Instant effect tokens:[/b]

[b]Intimidation Campaign[/b] - In our brave new world, social media are an optimal tool to scare society, ripe to use for someone like me! Using my associates' talents, I can spread some unnerving rumors on socials to raise the overall panic level.

[b]Destroy Evidence[/b] - Good, old-timey bonfire fueled by the things that would put you in prison (or asylum) can do miracles to lower the level of a military investigation. The investigators are not that bright, so it will take time for them to get back on track.

[b]Damage to the Military Base[/b] - Woops! Was something probably a little too explosive delivered to the military base? Maybe yes, maybe not, I of course don't know anything about it, but the military units in the district are sure to be moderately damaged now.

[b]Widespread Bombing Attacks[/b] - Sometimes you just have to go all out with the boom! Such a campaign from my associates is not delicate, but it does destroy all the military forces in the district, which makes it probably the most punch-packing Token. And an unfortunate drop in the district's population? Well, good thing I hate everyone in this city, however, it's a bit inconvenient for a scientist to suddenly have fewer test subjects available.

[b]Army Redeployment [/b]- The person who sent those orders might not be in fact the general whose signature seems to be on the papers. But hey, it makes all the military units move to other districts, making this one open for some mutant-assisted plunder.

[b]Migration Policies[/b] - All politicians in this damn city are corrupt to the bone and my associates know which strings to pull. Do you think you can't possibly move a large group of civilians to another district nearly instantaneously to increase the population there? Well, vote for someone other in the next elections.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/d748d44f5829cabbf900a5b27fcd1e796943aaff.gif[/img]

[i][b]Tokens with effects that last for one day:[/b]

[b]Battle Implants [/b]- Of course, my biotechnological solutions are far superior and more permanent but sometimes it's good to use a short-term boost to strength from these black market goodies. My mutants can deal 50% more damage in a target district for a day, and then probably live the rest of their unlife with some useless metal inside their bodies.

[b]Volunteer Support[/b] - If someone thought that you can volunteer only to do goodie two-shoes kind of things, they should think again. Just one overtly enthusiastic supporter of my "evil" cause can raise my creature's effectiveness in his district for a whole day.

[b]Distractions for the Army[/b] - Army people are very good at receiving orders, but very bad at anything that they need to solve without orders. Some shady maneuvers across their jurisdiction and they get confused, which makes them unable to detect my creatures in their district for a day.

[b]Army Munitions Sabotage[/b] - Something missing? For some of my associates stealing munitions from the army is a piece of the proverbial cake. The military can deal only half of their usual damage for a day and I wish I could see their stupid faces when they search for their missing bullets and rockets.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/36502232b031f653824bace5d62d81a462f55967.gif[/img]

[i]One more professional remark - regretfully, not all Dark Web assignments offer Tokens as a reward. Fortunately, the dealings in the underground are surprisingly open, so I can always check in the contract description what rewards it will yield.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
Here ends the 15th devlog for Creature Lab. Now you have an extended knowledge of what rewards from the Dark Web can exactly do for you. We hope you will use them to your hearts' content in the game!

notes.title: Scientist log - 014
notes.notes:
[i]The life of a brilliant scientist can be hard. The mockery of your peers, who don't understand your vision. The propaganda of your rivals, trying to discredit your work. The unhealthy interest of the military in your little mutant excursions. And that thing when your hair is always a mess, no matter how many times you try to get them sorted. But some of us take the hardships of life as a challenge and face them head-on with a smile![/i]

[h2]Difficulty levels in Creature Lab[/h2]

[i]Starting my experiments, I saw that my undoubted control of elements makes my work so much easier. When everything comes together as expected, I may focus on building up the bulk of my army. With an array of mass-produced mutagens, the military efforts seem to be just puny. [/i]

[quote]We wanted Creature Lab to be both accessible and challenging. That's why in the final game you will find three difficulty levels. The main difference between them lies in the chemistry and the interactions of the elements present in the substances you mix. To be more precise, the interactions of opposite elements are a key mechanic that will change between the difficulty levels - and also your capability of detecting the elements through analysis.[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/6f1f92d0dac6f22332cd57ecde295a16ada8a176.gif[/img] 

[i]But sometimes, chemistry won't collaborate. It's not easy to identify elements previously unknown to mankind. It's challenging to test their interactions, at least without accidental explosions. One must be very, very careful. Even if people technically may live twice with my help.[/i]

[quote]On [b]Normal[/b] difficulty, the opposite elements cancel themselves out but otherwise don't cause any harm. You can feed mutants with any potions (although those matching elements used to create it will be more effective), use any mutagens to grow limbs, and any potions to enhance the creature. The analysis of a substance under the microscope will always tell you exactly what elements it is composed of.

On [b]Hard [/b]difficulty, substance analysis changes significantly. Instead of one exact element, you get two possible elements. Only one is present in the mixture and you must figure out which one it is... by experimenting as a scientist would.[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/238a654c1b474ee25015bd81e10a73af7ec8fb01.gif[/img]

[i]Frankly, I heard people calling me insane too many times. Yadda, Yadda, boring... But there are challenges for master biochemists that just cannot be described in other words. Insanity may be elementary here if you excuse a poor pun.[/i]

[quote]The truly twisted chemical challenge awaits you at [b]Insane [/b]difficulty. Now opposite elements don't cancel themselves - using them in one mixture automatically results in unusable sludge (disgusting!). On Insane, you have to nourish and enhance mutants only with potions that don't have any elements opposite to the creature's elements. The same rule applies to making new limbs.

In addition, the chemist's guessing game is even harder this time. Analyzing the substance gives you three possible elements of which it may be composed. You need to figure out which exactly is in there by mixing and matching. This boils down to mixing the substances/elixirs with the known elements in it with those with unknown elements. By their reaction, you can learn the composition of the latter. With opposites in mind, this may be a rather painstakingly difficult process.[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/f1982f26e9e010f59174d2c88055374175c83446.gif[/img]

And with this, we have reached the end of our 14th devlog. Now you should have an idea about how you can ramp up the challenge in the final version of Creature Lab. It's good to mention that all levels are described in detail So who'll be brave enough to tackle Insane? 😉

notes.title: Scientist log - 013
Scientist log - 012
notes.notes:
[i]As a man of science, I never intended to go to war. My goal is revolution. Still, those tend to not be bloodless. My mutants can move silently, but on the other hand, they will always stand out. A view of a corpse with giant sword-like appendages will always be alarming. One person that will alert the authorities is enough to start a skirmish with the police or even the military. To win a war, one needs to know its rules. So I learned everything about clashing with those who I view as mere obstacles on the way to scientific progress. [/i]

[h2]Rules of combat[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/eb0d9ef0f1742bd5c252d6eeaad423b6c33c22cd.gif[/img]

[i]The first and most important rule to remember is that I am already out of control when combat happens. I don't always like it that way, but I can't accompany my creatures to their missions. You should never put such kind of genius as mine at risk.

In such a case, preparation is the key. Before the mission, I always click on the selected district on my ingenious digital city map. There I can view how many police and military units are stationed in the district. It is also divided by type: light tactical units, anti-terrorists, tanks, mechanized infantry, and police. This way I know exactly the size and capabilities of a potential combat force my mutants will face. This allows one to plan the encounter accordingly, selecting mutants with the right statistics, skills, and bonuses.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/a3a98595ff623af04f100ae4ef6af616c3c27928.gif[/img]

[i]Each encounter is viewed in the special software of my secret computer as a visualization, which shows all of my mutants and all of the enemies. The combat engagement is presented in three phases for me to easily follow the events. Which units will attack in which phase is determined by their abilities. In phase one only Ranged and melee units with Fast will trade blows. The second phase is an out battle between all the units, including units with no special ability (such as normal melee mutants) except those with Slow. In the third phase, all the remaining units will fight, joined by those with Slow.

As for trading blows, the general priority of attacking in combat is targeting the Fast units first, standard monsters and military second, and Slow units last. In most cases, the Fast units on both sides will be wiped out first. Ranged units are the only units with the ability to target even those units which haven't joined the fight yet. Slow units are the safest, but they attack only on the tall end of the fight.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/33d2d040fbb8353889c20542649c89080a085024.gif[/img]

[i]There are many nuances to combat, but two things I consider worth remembering. The first is that the damage is randomized based on units of minimal and maximal damage. The second is that the third phase is a bit different. The first two phases have only one round of fighting, after which the remaining units move to the next phase. The third phase will have as many rounds as needed to announce the victory of one side or the other - the units will fight till no units with vitality over zero remain on one side. This also means that if the military/police win, I lose all mutants. I made a habit of always checking the Degree of Danger bar on the Mission screen before I sent out the creatures to avoid such an unfavorable outcome.[/i]

[hr][/hr] 
This was our twelfth regular [b]“Scientist Log”[/b]. Combat is ultimately the thing the creatures are designed for, so experiment with the variety of options when you do missions, to know which composition of units is best suited to punish the military stationing in a particular district,

notes.title: Scientist log - 011
notes.notes:
[i]Creating new limbs for my creatures is not always an easy process. Each limb can grant a permanent boost to their power, but also unique abilities, which make the monster specialized in certain kinds of combat situations. Thankfully, the incubator I've constructed is useful in indicating how the limb will turn out and what its strengths will be.[/i]

[h2]Effects of the limb transplant[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/13277588b8734da58010c7ee06710ebab71d9df2.gif[/img]

[i]The first thing I must always, always remember is that the limb will be only compatible with the mutant I extracted the DNA from. May seem obvious, but when you have an army, you may sometimes forget which sample you have loaded in a rush! I must add the DNA sequence may be chosen from a menu on the incubator laptop and loaded anytime once I extracted it from the creature. Oh, and I of course always need to have enough mutagen on hand to incubate a limb - from one to even three doses!

It's important to not have to experiment blindly every time you need to make a little replacement. That's why I can select a kind of limb that I want to grow straight from the menu of the incubator laptop by using the UP and DOWN arrows on the screen. The choice of unusual and deadly appendages is quite varied! [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/bcf0325608865074a065b1818a1a28ce5ac5750d.gif[/img]

[i]On the right side of the screen, there is a list of bonuses that the limb will provide if attached to the creature. There are three categories of them:
[list]
[*] Vitality Bonus - an increase in mutant's health,
[*] Min Damage - plus to the minimum of damage the creature will inflict on enemies
[*] Max Damage - plus to the minimum of damage the creature will inflict on enemies
[/list]
Thanks to this I can easily calculate how the limb swap will affect the statistics of my monster- and plan out which limbs should I attach for the desired effects. But there is also a mysterious label that reads ABILITIES. Well, in nature limbs come in pairs and even abominations against nature can benefit from pairing their appendages. Pairs of certain limbs can grant the mutant special abilities, that make it more effective in dealing with specific situations or enemies. Those are described in the ABILITIES window.
[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/ab783594ae972216f36dc016ad552c6576f00bb2.gif[/img]

[i]Abilities that I can grant to the creature via transplanting a pair of the same limbs (left and right) are:
[list]
[*] Fast - allows the creature to start fighting enemies in the first wave attack even without ranged ability, but it also takes damage first,
[*] Slow - the creature takes damage after other mutants and starts fighting only in the third phase of attacks when it is less vulnerable than monsters without this ability,
[*] Ranged - the creature can attack in every phase of combat and even enemies that haven't engaged in fighting yet,
[/list]
Additionally, two of the arms are vital to countering enemy abilities:
[list]
[*] Ax limb - makes the creature deal additional damage to enemies with Armored ability, such as tanks or mechanized infantry,
[*] Pliers limb - makes the creature deal additional damage to enemies with Light ability, such as the police, anti-terrorists, or light tactical units.
[/list]
Equipping monsters with such limbs can make them an invaluable asset, which can even save my army in case of a violent clash with security forces. I like to have many tactical options and, as always, my genius delivers in this area.
[/i]
[hr][/hr] 
This was our eleventh regular [b]“Scientist Log”[/b]. We hope this extended look at how limbs enhance your creations made you already plan some wild combinations. Certainly, those blades, claws, and... frog legs make mutants not only better but also more interesting to look at (and panic about).

notes.title: Scientist Log - 010
notes.notes:
[i]All of my work, as with every breakthrough scientific experiment, is susceptible to an element of chance. Every substance I make is brand new, and every mutant has different capabilities. Thus, you need to control this randomness. But that's what science is for. Thanks to my ingenious computer system, I can track the abilities of my creations - and nourish them with substances that will further evolve them![/i]

[h2][b]Mutant Statistics[/b][/h2]

[i]Thanks to the vast Creatureopedia, which saves all the data on my new creation nearly instantly, I can take a look at unique qualities, which I categorized for my convenience. They immediately tell me what the mutant is capable of and what its weak point is.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/b96a8bc44ac319f80d89f002a469f7814b01566c.gif[/img]

[i]The two most important statistics are Vitality and Efficiency. They are affected by the missions, so I have to be aware of them for each mutant to assign them to the task accordingly. Vitality is showing the life spark in the creature and zeroing this stat means its (second) death. Vitality is lost primarily in combat. Efficiency is indicating how well the creature is doing its tasks during missions. You can think of it as a mutant's stamina. Each mission takes a percentage of the state and when it reaches zero, you cannot send the creature to the city.  

Both Vitality and Efficiency can be regained only by nourishing the creature with new mutagens. Alternatively, I can always dispose of it...[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/2c463b54820ab7cbb4db262da674af2977ff31fb.gif[/img]

[i]But that's not the end. Among the statistics I've categorized are secondary statistics, which are an important indicator of a specific mutant's capabilities. The key to successfully performing missions is to use the strengths the creature has to its advantage.

[b]Substance Acquisition[/b] - the talent of bringing me so much-needed substances stolen in the city.
[b]Body Acquisition -[/b] the mutant needs to have some skill in stealing the bodies... and bringing them back relatively intact.
[b]Terror [/b]- this measures how scary is the creature to the public and how fast its sudden appearance on the streets will raise panic.
[b]Stealth [/b]- combat situations are usually not optimal, so the ability to lurk around avoiding detection is crucial to my endeavors. 
[b]Anti-Light Attacks[/b] - the ability to counter the attacks of infantry.
[b]Armor Piercing Attacks [/b]- the ability to handle tanks and other heavy military equipment.[/i]
[i][b]Vitality Boost [/b]- the bonus to Vitality from the mutagens used on the creature
[b]Efficiency  Boost [/b]- the bonus to Efficiency from the mutagens used on the creature[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/4696018db7363010a7b24173dbd21ad12f2a7fe9.gif[/img]

[i]Of course, a genius like me has a method of raising the creature's statistics. One is just "feeding" them new mutagens, which can unleash the additional potential in them. I can also develop new limbs from mutant DNA. Those are especially needed to raise the combat potential of the monster. 

Additionally, I devised a genius method to grow new internal organs in my lab. By replacing the lungs, the stomach, or the liver of a creature, one can discover valuable boosts, which elevate its usefulness. Those boosts often need a certain substance to be activated properly,[/i]

[hr][/hr] 
This was our tenth regular [b]“Scientist Log”[/b]. The statistics of the mutants allow you to plan your missions. The Creatureopedia is a great way to keep each of your creations on track. We hope you have a clear idea of how statistics will work in the game now. Remember that you can also talk with us directly via Discord:

notes.title: An update on the Creature Lab release timings
notes.notes:
Hello,

We are aware that many of you are eagerly awaiting the confirmation of a new release date for Creature Lab. Thank you for all your inquiries on that topic, which show us that you are very engaged in our game. We have also promised to provide more details as soon as possible and today we deliver an update on this topic.

According to our estimates, [b]Creature Lab needs over a month of additional work[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/a7f88612a3c34028fd20a29bf43d29b32007ba5a.jpg[/img]

First of all, we'd like to explain further the main reason for the delay. While we were working on the missing localizations, we discovered that the mission system implemented in the game is interacting wrongly with the save system. In several specific instances, it could lead to corrupted save files. This of course made us unable to release the game according to our quality standards, so we decided to take our time and make the necessary adjustments. We want you to enjoy a stable version of Creature Lab when it launches.

Currently, we are replacing the existing mission system with a new one. [b]To implement it properly and do several necessary rounds of QA testing, we need roughly 6 weeks or so.[/b]

Of course, this estimate is subject to change, as the process of changing the game is not always progressing ideally. But we trust that eventual changes will be minimal.

Based on that production estimate, we aim to announce the new release date somewhere around early March, as soon as everything is ready and we find a suitable release window. The time between the release date announcement and the actual release will be short. Hopefully, both events will happen in the same month.

As we stated before, we don't want to predict the actual date before we're sure that it's rock solid and unmoveable. We are very grateful for your kind words on the delay here on Steam and elsewhere on our comms channels and hope today's update clarifies our plans.

[h2][b]We implement more changes for your enjoyment![/b]

As we ensured, we use the added time wisely and implement quality-of-life changes in addition to improving the core systems. Such changes are, as usual, based on your feedback from the demo and our other presentations. The occasion calls for a sneak peek.

notes.title: We are postponing the launch of Creature Lab
notes.notes:
Dear fans and aspiring mad scientists,
 
It’s always hard to come forward with bad news and double hard to repeat a bad message. We truly respect your dedication to Creature Lab and how eager you are to jump into the role of crazy professor raising his army of relentless mutants. We are also super eager to let you try the result of our long, sometimes harsh, but passionate work. Creature Lab is everything to us, together with its community.
 
However, life is rarely made of ideal situations. And developing a game as an independent team can be a perfect example of this truth sometimes.
 
[b]That’s why, after much consideration, we regretfully inform you that we have to postpone the game yet again.[/b]
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/c5e843d5f01381fddfb214ebf4c66b6f6bdce9c1.jpg[/img]

We know you already have a lot of doubts about this delay, and the number one question is: why? One big reason is the process of localization to all languages we have committed to making available at launch. [b]Despite the best efforts of both us and our translation partners, we found significant parts of localized versions not on par with our quality standard. We need some time to get them to the level of polish we can present to native speakers without any doubt.[/b]
 
As for the second reason, it may feel like repeating the reasons behind our previous delay. However, Creature Lab became a, well, really big creature during the development process. [b]We have implemented all the features and systems we wanted to include in the launch build. However. we were not fully satisfied with the way they work and interact in some aspects.[/b]

We want Creature Lab to be not just playable. We aim to deliver the best possible experience for all of the players. [b]That’s why we decided to give those features more time for additional polish. We are sure this will make them more fun to use in the final game.[/b]
 
So we’re taking some time to provide the best final touch possible. [b]As we have to make you wait a little bit more for a second time, we don’t want to commit to a date that is not written in stone. For the moment, we are setting the game to Coming Soon status.[/b]

That doesn’t mean that we intend to make you wait a second longer than needed. [b]We hope to provide you with an unmovable, ultimate launch date as soon as possible.[/b] And we mean to put focus on the word „soon”.
 
Of course, we are here to answer your questions. Don’t hesitate to ask us anything via Discord and Steam discussions. Let’s start a conversation and we’ll be sure to address your doubts and feedback.
 
[b]We’re sorry again and thank you for your patience! You make our work worthwhile and we promise to bring you the most abominable (by this we mean the best) version of Creature Lab possible in this universe![/b]

notes.title: Scientist Log – 009
notes.notes:
[i]Working alone is tied to the specifics of my experiments by definition. I am always in the shadows since our “normal” society has no understanding of my scientific pursuits and my refusal of being limited by conventions and so-called ethics. I cannot trust anyone – but sometimes, you can find certain organizations also operating in this shadowy underground, which can put my creations to good use. And I can put the resources they can provide to even better use.

That is why I am always connected to the...

[h2]Dark Web[/h2]

This part of the internet is inaccessible to the uninitiated, where people with very specific and very illegal needs seek the services of eager creative minds like myself.

Funnily enough, the system which is used to post Dark Web contracts is similar to a message board that could be found on the “normie” internet. I can access it from my hidden computer system, which I also use to coordinate missions in the city. By selecting [b]MSGBOARD[/b], I get to access a list of contracts from many different shadowy organizations: “evil” corporations, fringe science initiatives, cults, revolutionary movements, and many other entities beyond the knowledge of the public. They are grouped into several factions. With time, there are more and more contracts appearing on the message board. You can also see the type of goods you need to deliver and rewards in the form of symbols next to each contract.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/2e6781a9048fc9a41ffc4e0c00c2e853d862d4bd.gif[/img]

Of course, when I open a specific contract, I can see the needs of the employer in more detail. Those can fall into several categories. The employer may ask for mutagens with required properties. They may also order me to deliver one of my custom-made limbs or even a whole mutant creature with a certain set of those. 

However, I have to mind time constraints. There is always a set deadline to deliver the goods – and you can also find sprint contracts, which have a very strict time limit. Sometimes they will be done only if I already had the required resources stored in your lab. If I fail the contract, I will lose my reputation with the employer’s faction, which means fewer contracts from them and fewer rewards for a set period. However, if I’m doing well with a faction, I will get more contracts with stronger rewards. So you need to strategize and set priorities when taking up any of those jobs. If I decide to accept a contract, it disappears from the message board and lands in a separate [b]ORDERS[/b] menu, from which I can monitor them and deliver the requested resources.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/7ada1170dc44cae94c5688b5d8511ff1ebee3f88.gif[/img]

But what do I get out of those contracts? The employers offer me the most needed things for my experiments – new substances and dead bodies – and they are great alternative sources for those. This allows me to put my mutants in harm’s way less often to bring them from the city. But perhaps the most valuable rewards are tokens. Tokens are single-use “favors” I can gain from different factions through contracts and select from a separate [b]TOKEN[/b] menu. They vary from special implants that can temporarily strengthen my creatures, to sabotaging the army bases, destroying evidence of my presence in the city, or even getting volunteers to help with my missions. Some stronger tokens are specific to one faction, so you have to keep your reputation in check and take up advanced contracts to access them. Tokens usually take effect immediately, although some provide bonuses lasting one day.
[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/4658a6d6e0cc9abad8eb0ab575e9a9aee83ce4ae.gif[/img]

[hr][/hr] 
This was our ninth regular [b]“Scientist Log”[/b]. As you can see, Dark Web is a great addition that works as an optional side quest system, from which you can immensely benefit during your quest for The Ultimate Mutagen. It adds such a fun layer to the gameplay that we dedicated a separate stretch goal in our Kickstarter campaign for an extended edition (running till January 10th) to a mobile Dark Web app. If you want to help us make it a reality, you can support our Kickstarter linked below:

notes.title: Scientist log - 008
notes.notes:
[i]Every great mind likes fun toys. Especially if they are used for science. I am no exception to this rule and there is a handful of objects that I collected to make my life as a genius a bit easier and more convenient. Of course, I talk about the...

[h2]New Lab Equipment[/h2]

Let's start with my Automated Speedy Mutagen Mixing Multiplifaction Station (side note - need to work on shorter invention names). In its most basic form, it simply allows me to combine 4 different ingredients at the same time, making it more convenient compared to my old alembic. Brewing mutagens has never been this fast!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/e8505ab50ce2f1a04df6a08fa75f7921081cf2fd.gif[/img]

But this is just a fraction of Automated Speedy Mutagen Mixing Multiplifaction Station's true potential! If I install a few upgrades I can even multiply anything I create with this equipment! I just need to use some obsolete substance, something I don't need, and pour it into the side containers. My machine will use them to make more copies of the 4 ingredients in my primary chambers. Without this invention, I would need at least 12 ingredients to make 3 mutagens. If I install it, I will only need 6! 4 of them will form the mutagen while 2 extras will be destroyed to create two more copies of my mutagen. Now that's efficiency!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/beb3027b67d34bc665f33e83a5c13e3f2f8910df.jpg[/img]

In my work, I sometimes get a little... overzealous with my experiments. And I can't afford to have my laboratory flooded with useless failed experiments. To deal with the garbage problem, I locked my old pet in a metal safe. It doesn't quite fit but that's even better - it means that I don't have to open it up to feed the pet. I can just throw it some unnecessary experiments and it will happily dispose of the waste!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/cece57083d96f51bb541306c0d27c89a8238bf34.gif[/img]

Speaking of disposal... While my creations are brilliant, I sometimes can't afford the luxury of keeping them all. My creatures get tired with every mission and they get injured if the military discovers them. I need to feed them more mutagen to cure their wounds. But if I am starved for resources, I can pick a creature to sacrifice and recover some of the ingredients I used while making it. The process is quite irreversible but can be used as a last resort.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/65885726f3fbdfade34b21df4a45bb1d0f9a5880.gif[/img]
[/i]
[hr][/hr] 
The above is our eighth "[b]Scientist Log[/b]". As you can see, we added a faster way of making mutagens. This feature was implemented as a result of yet another feedback that we got from YOU - the community. Thank you for your brilliant suggestions and we encourage you to post more!

notes.title: Scientist log - 007
notes.notes:
[i]There is no limit to greatness. Nothing stops me from bending the laws of physics and making a creature so powerful that even a modern tank is no match for it. As long as I have enough resources to spare, I can even consider...

[h2]Creature Enhancement[/h2]

The idea is straightforward. If a single mutagen can animate a corpse and make it outperform a regular human in practically every field that matters, then can I increase the dosage or add a new mutagen altogether?

Early experiments clearly demonstrated that giving a creature a radically different mutagen from the one they were made with results in a complete waste of time and requires thorough cleaning. But a genius like me doesn't get discouraged by small setbacks! Instead, I tried administering small doses of compatible elixirs and mutagens into select organs of my specimens. And the result was incredible!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/ece3ced051cd5d411b22329cc266f9c3936e9ad4.gif[/img]

This enhancement method is very effective but, unfortunately, temporary. The subject loses its potency roughly a day after administering any additional elixirs or mutagens. Nevertheless, a genius only needs a day to change the world!

It's fascinating how even every component of the injection has an effect on my creatures. And the effect changes depending on the place of injection! Fascinating! I already mapped out some of the interactions and I can't wait to figure out the rest of them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/44fc6c945a43be2f2fe61713bcc014d25007e7ee.jpg[/img]

Of course, like with any experiment on an active creature, I must be very careful when handling my beauties. For they do not like when I mess with them too much. And they can get... quite angry.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/b94ac48592240f093dd39c13a9fa4d199b65b22a.gif[/img]
[/i]
[hr][/hr] 
The above is our seventh '[b]Scientist Log[/b]'. A deep dive into the enhancement mechanic plus a small spoiler of what you can do with enhancements. We decided to tease out a few select combinations so that you know what to expect from the system. But we kept most of the combinations secret so you have to play the game to fill out the blanks!

notes.title: Scientist log - 006
notes.notes:
[i]Even the best computer can run out of space. Thus, it is unsurprising that the best human can also run out of space - the brain space, where I keep all my formulas and accomplishments. Truth is, if you are responsible for thousands of incredible creations like I am, you will need a place to store information about them.

Which is why I have my handy...
[h2]Monster & Substance Encyclopedias[/h2]

They are largely automated and while there are some differences between the two of them, the concept is the same. Every time I make a discovery, it gets added to my encyclopedia. There, I can browse all of my discoveries, filter them, sort them, and search them, much like I do when I order mortuary fridges online.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/d3086accaa7fa3c63c33b99b51f772274904e4e2.gif[/img]

Of course, there are some limitations. Even I can't always predict the effectiveness of my wonderful creatures. So when I first create a new strain of helper, their stats are unknown. But once I send them on a mission, my incredible encyclopedia will make miraculous analyses of the creature's performance and note its effectiveness! Clever, isn't it?

Things are no different for my mutagen encyclopedia. I don't always know what composition a new mutagen has. So the encyclopedia just lists all possible elements and it's up to me to conduct further experiments and figure out what exactly I created. Once I have a theory in place, I can mark my assumed elements on the mixture's encyclopedia page.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/259e212ecd680f82a42aff48fe0d7a552d954677.gif[/img]

Overall, these tools really improve my workflow and ensure that I can focus on my genius creations without having to worry about cataloging them all.
[/i]
[hr][/hr] 
The above is our sixth "[b]Scientist Log[/b]". A way to track created potions was our #1 request from the playtest we launched earlier this year. We hope that the encyclopedias will cover that need! They are fully implemented now and we just need to do a bit of visual touch-up ;)

As excellent as my creations are, they are no match for reinforced steel or powerful explosives. At least not by default. As the military starts to increase its presence in the city, I need to take extra steps to protect my work... and myself.

I can collect a DNA sample of any of my minions and create a brand new limb tailored to them. These new limbs enhance the battle properties of a mutant and allow it to take on powerful foes... maybe even [b]armored troop transports[/b] or [b]tanks[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/c217d5602d8dae09be6e73aa46ac16bb1e994176.gif[/img]

Creating a new limb requires generous use of mutagens so I should do it only once I gather a decent stockpile of them. I also have to ensure that this limb is created with a mutagen that matches a mutant the limb is meant for. Otherwise, the shock might cause my creation to [b]expire prematurely[/b].

Every limb has different properties. By changing the legs, I can make a sturdy monster faster, so that it takes the shots which would destroy other creatures. By changing the limbs I can make a minion capable of [b]ranged attacks[/b]. I can prepare for every situation, as long as I plan in advance - as it takes a few days to grow some of the more powerful appendages.

But the result - oh, the result is definitely worth it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/c68ac57dc63ab5f524ea06649d6dd71c284c72ca.gif[/img]

[/i]

notes.title: Scientist log - 004
notes.notes:
[i]The most important lesson I learned over the years is: you cannot do it alone. Even if you're a genius working on your eighth thesis, you still need help to deal with the mundane stuff.

Although I am not only mentally but also physically excellent, I still cannot be in many places at once. I need servants to do my bidding. People to fetch me the ingredients I need, deal with the annoying investigators, or "recruit" more test subjects. And ideally, they shouldn't ask any questions. Thankfully, my research means that I don't need to recruit actual people. My lab-grown mutants will do.

[h2]Monster Creation[/h2]

My beautiful creations can take care of my errands while I focus my attention on science. My brilliant mutagens can animate corpses and morph them into more practical shapes. What they lack in intelligence, they make up for in brawn. If I send one of my mutants to fetch me some reagents, it might not bring me [i]exactly [/i]what I want, but it will still bring me more stuff than I could otherwise gather.

Of course, my incredible mutagens alone won't do the trick. As explained above, I need a body to morph into a proper monster. Thankfully, fresh corpses are never difficult to acquire. Especially when you have an army of mutants at your command.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/6a3e17a38e99c6ad6d421e31f317ce574431b0ba.gif[/img]

Once I have a body to alter, the rest of the process is relatively straightforward. I designed a [b]mutation chamber[/b] where I can place a fresh corpse. Then I just need to fill the tanks with mutagen and start the process. Any mutagen will do but I best remember what mutagen was used. My creations act differently, depending on the substance that was used to mutate them. 

Of course, caution is advised during the entire process. Should I forget to sedate a freshly made monster, they might even turn on me and attack!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/f5c79c38ae9b536067522f74490b041b3dfec581.gif[/img]

While creating a new creature is easier than discovering new mutagens, where my genius truly shines is the endless possibilities that monster creation entails. Firstly, the choice of the mutagen can infuse my servants with supernatural strength or unmatched reflexes. And secondly, I can further enhance my monsters by feeding them more mutagen or by [b]changing their limbs[/b]! But this is a whole separate topic...[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/c68ac57dc63ab5f524ea06649d6dd71c284c72ca.gif[/img]

[hr][/hr] 
The above is our fourth "[b]Scientist Log[/b]". Monster creation is meant to be a simple and satisfying process, a bit of a breather after difficult experiments in the lab. Upon their creation, monsters gain a bonus to stats enhanced by a mutagen that the player used. This bonus is permanent and determines what a given creature is going to be best at.

notes.title: Scientist log - 003
notes.notes:
[i]It's one thing to randomly combine different ingredients in hope of making something great. It's a completely different thing to purposefully analyze different substances to achieve exactly what is needed.

Sadly, the foolish masses that form governments and corporations are too ignorant to appreciate my genius and fund my research. This means that I need to be very careful with my reagents. They're not easy to get. Every drop wasted on unnecessary experiments is a step away from my ultimate goal. In order to avoid this, I must spend adequate time...

[h2]Testing substances[/h2]

The idea is brilliant in its simplicity. In order to avoid wasting precious reagents, I must [b]analyze every reaction[/b] and write down the results. Then I can cross-reference them with other reactions and figure out how to brew efficient and powerful mutagens.

And how does one analyze their mixtures?
[olist]
[*] Mix two different ones. It's best to start with something simple, like mixing two ingredients.
[*] Analyze the result under a microscope!
[*] Draw preliminary conclusions.
[*] Mix the result with some other ingredient and check what effect it had.
[/olist]
And so on, and so forth...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/7154d59d8e14c8083be7b1d85e73a60e8cd898e9.png[/img]

Pictured above is the [b]analyzing screen[/b]. In its center, you can see the substance that's being analyzed. The bottom right corner displays the ingredients that were used to brew the mixture. The upper right corner is where I keep my notes, although my computer system also generates some for me.

As you can see, there isn't much useful information here... yet. But I can already draw some conclusions. For instance, my unparalleled intellect is telling me that the cells pictured in the middle are caused by an activator. Good, I need an activator to brew mutagens. However, this particular substance is not a mutagen - my computer system ascertained that it's not complex enough to be a mutagen. Must be an elixir then.

The next step is to add another ingredient or elixir to this one and see what happens.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/e91b5b78ca5a5877921ddc9b0227688c0801ae59.png[/img]

A most satisfactory result, a mutagen! I must make note of the ingredients that I used so I can recreate this mutagen in the future. Now, there is no way of figuring out what effect it has exactly but it's certainly worth injecting it into a test subject to figure this out.

Another option is to add yet another ingredient and see what effect it might have.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/2c683cd891694fac059de573f42b34df384572f1.png[/img]

Whatever it is I added, it seems to have downgraded my mutagen back into a regular elixir. All of the activator cells seem to be missing. An ignorant might consider this a failure. For me, this is a spectacular success!

It means that whatever substance I used was the opposite of the previous activator. [b]Every substance has two states[/b] - positive and negative. Mix them together and they cancel each other out. What's important is that positive activators create far more powerful mutagens than negative activators.

My computer already made the assumption that Gaxili must be an activator and it must be opposite to Snow Anise. I do happen to have a bit more of Gaxili and if I add it to my current substance...

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/4a58b8c585dad77e1a0a799f640bacf37944cfbc.gif[/img]

I end up with a very, very powerful mutagen indeed. I can tell by just looking at it. From now on, I will always grab Gaxili whenever I can and create truly magnificent creatures![/i]

notes.title: Scientist Log - 002
notes.notes:
[i]I must hide.

It's all because of the government. Or the corporations. I'm not even sure exactly. But some short-sighted fools refuse to acknowledge my genius and actively hinder my research. I have no choice, I must find a new place where I can conduct my experiments in peace.

[h2]My secret laboratory[/h2]

I will miss my old lab a bit but it was about time I move anyway. My experiments require a lot of space after all and my previous accommodation just wouldn't cut it. Let's see, I need a place to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1309990/view/5438635396033667386]mix my elixirs and mutagens[/url], that's obvious. I will also need a storeroom for new ingredients, new equipment, and of course, some test subjects. Once I have bodies to experiment on and mutagens to use, I will need a secure room to conduct my experiments. And a place where I can plan my future actions... Hold up, this list is getting long, let's plan things out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/bbfbae7da7d550bf8dd4aad8bdf4acb26fa9d364.png[/img]

There we go! This layout should work. In order to keep up the appearance of a law-abiding citizen, I will prepare an atrium in [b]section A[/b]. I could use an office anyway, I should be able to plan my next moves there.

I shall dedicate [b]section B[/b] as my storeroom. It has plenty of power outlets, so I can keep my test subjects refrigerated. I think there are some body fridges at the abandoned hospital on the outskirts of the city. Maybe they still work.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/33608a4eac33a131672ea05a47bcf7110f3860a7.jpg[/img]

[b]Section C[/b] is where I will work on my concoctions and other projects that do not require a specimen. Using some scrap I had available, I was able to build a prototype of a new appendage incubation station. I should be able to use it to create stronger body parts with unique features. This will be a difficult and complicated process and I will detail it sometime later.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/7875ded6e0de18ff298c89f0eedde40cca0dbac5.jpg[/img]

My most brilliant work will take place in [b]section D[/b], where I animate my beautiful creations! I will need some very advanced equipment for the final mutations. My retrofitted industrial laser will also need to fit in there, the same goes for some other bulky lab equipment I use. Yes, this will have to be a big, spacious room. I likely won't have enough space for the standard security measures but a genius like me won't need them anyway.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/4b737bdf1005bc577445088c8dface321e2d511c.jpg[/img]

Yes, I think I have the basics covered. There is still some equipment I need to obtain and I should start moving my gear to a new spot. It is a shame that I must do so now, I despise such repetitive, obnoxious work. But science is a cruel mistress and I understand the necessity of preparations before proper experiments can commence.[/i]

notes.title: Scientist Log - 001
notes.notes:
[i]They never appreciated me. They never understood my genius. But now... now I will prove their insignificance to them!

Work is busy, here in my lab. After someone [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wZG8sAvUAsk]posted what I do on the Internet[/url], I had to pick up the pace and organize my approach. From this point forth, I shall write detailed logs on the progress I've made... for posterity.

[h2]Let's begin with the mixtures![/h2]

Yes, my precious mixtures. So colorful, so beautiful. So powerful. There are three types of mixtures, you see. There are, of course, [b]ingredients[/b]. The most basic of basics, each containing just one aspect. One is not nearly enough but we all have to start somewhere, don't we? I can find these ingredients anywhere in the city but I usually don't occupy myself with the tedious task of acquiring them and send out my minions to grab what I need. That's far more efficient!

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/1eedf01b01952bb6a332e5ed075635e6f91abdb6.gif[/img]

But what happens when you mix two different ingredients, you might ask. Well, as one might expect, if you do this properly, you receive something that contains not one but two aspects. I tend to call such a mixture, an [b]elixir[/b]. In theory, there is no limit to how complex an elixir might be. It could have just two aspects or it could three or it could have six! The only issue is finding the right equipment to brew such complex elixirs... I'm afraid that my current laboratory just doesn't cut it beyond a certain point. Ah, I should really upgrade my lab but how can I waste my precious time when there's more science to do?

But I'm getting ahead of myself. Even the most complex elixirs are, frankly, useless. Scientifically speaking, they are incredible, but they just aren't enough to create more minions. You see, aspects alone just don't cut it. You need something more - an activator. Difficult to acquire, certainly. But without it, I simply cannot reanimate my minions. The activator is the key.

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39596769/e55626d04da7a95b84b869b09ef7f5792846f2bf.gif[/img]

So, what do you get if you mix an elixir with three aspects and an ingredient with an activator? The answer is - a [b]mutagen[/b]! The very key to my success! Mutagens are the bread and butter of reputable scientists such as myself. They practically do all the work for me. And depending on the aspects contained within a mutagen, I can create all sorts of wonderful monstrosities to do my bidding! Super strength? Easy! Unrivaled agility? Not even a challenge! An intellect that could rival mine... well, that's obviously not possible but you get the idea.

Of course, discovering the most potent mutagen of all does require a bit of trial and error. Even I can't always predict how my chosen ingredients will mix. And I'm certain that if there was another, parallel universe, the same ingredients could even contain entirely different aspects! Just think about the endless possibilities! 

If that doesn't excite you, I don't know what will.[/i]
